Question 3

Explain why the standard deviation is NA for one carrier, and why it is 0 for others. Demonstrate your answer using code.

The standard deviation is NA when there is only one observation and 0 when all the observations are equal for that carrier.

flights %>%
  filter(month == 1) %>%
  filter(carrier %in% c("OO", "YV", "F9", "AS")) %>%
  group_by(carrier, distance) %>%
  summarise(observations = n(), .groups = "drop")
# A tibble: 4 × 3
  carrier distance observations
  <chr>      <dbl>        <int>
1 AS          2402           62
2 F9          1620           59
3 OO           733            1
4 YV           229           46

Question 4

Using tidyr and dplyr where appropriate, construct a dataframe where the carriers are along the columns, and the rows are the average departure delay (dep_delay) flown by each carrier (carrier) in each month.

flights %>%
  group_by(month, carrier) %>%
  summarise(avg_dep_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = carrier, values_from = avg_dep_delay)

Question 5

Calculate the proportion of flights that were delayed (dep_delay greater than 0) but arrived on or before time (arr_delay less than or equal to 0).

flights %>%
  summarise(proportion = mean(dep_delay > 0 & arr_delay <= 0, na.rm = TRUE))
# A tibble: 1 × 1
  proportion
       <dbl>
1      0.108

Question 6

Using the airlines and flights datasets, do the following, showing the output from each step:

  • Identify routes that more than one airline flies
routes <- flights %>%
  group_by(origin, dest) %>%
  summarise(num_carriers = n_distinct(carrier), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(num_carriers > 1) %>%
  select(origin, dest)

  • For each such route, calculate the average arrival delay for each airline (exclude NAs). Find the names of these airlines.
avg_delays <- routes %>%
  inner_join(flights, by = c("origin", "dest")) %>%
  group_by(origin, dest, carrier) %>%
  summarise(avg_arr_delay = mean(arr_delay, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(airlines, by = "carrier") %>%
  relocate(name, .before = avg_arr_delay)

  • For each such route, identify the airline with the worst and best average arrival delay.
best_worst <- avg_delays %>%
  group_by(origin, dest) %>%
  summarise(worst_airline = name[which.max(avg_arr_delay)],
            worst_arr_delay = max(avg_arr_delay),
            best_airline = name[which.min(avg_arr_delay)],
            best_arr_delay = min(avg_arr_delay),
            .groups = "drop")

  • Identify the route with the greatest difference between the best and worst performing airlines
best_worst <- best_worst %>%
  mutate(arr_delay_diff = worst_arr_delay - best_arr_delay) %>%
  arrange(desc(arr_delay_diff))

head(best_worst, n = 1)

  origin dest  worst_airline         worst_arr_delay best_airline best_arr_delay

1 JFK    ATL   ExpressJet Airlines …             128 Endeavor Ai…           1.40
# ℹ 1 more variable: arr_delay_diff <dbl>
  • Determine the reason for this difference
flights %>%
  filter(origin == "JFK", dest == "ATL") %>%
  group_by(carrier) %>%
  summarise(num_flights = n(),
            avg_arr_delay = mean(arr_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
            avg_dep_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
            dep_arr_diff = avg_arr_delay - avg_dep_delay,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(airlines, by = "carrier") %>%
  relocate(carrier, name)
# A tibble: 3 × 6
  carrier name              num_flights avg_arr_delay avg_dep_delay dep_arr_diff
  <chr>   <chr>                   <int>         <dbl>         <dbl>        <dbl>
1 9E      Endeavor Air Inc.          55          1.40          1.47      -0.0679
2 DL      Delta Air Lines …        1874          6.34         10.7       -4.32  
3 EV      ExpressJet Airli…           1        128           124          4

ExpressJet Airlines only flew the JFK to ATL route once and it was delayed by 2 hours and 4 minutes. It is not necessarily the worst airline since the difference between arrival and departure is only 4 minutes compared to 0 minutes from Endeavor Air. But the large difference between the airlines arrival delays is due to ExpressJet departing 2 hours late and Endeavor by only 1 minute.
